ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Pablo Neruda Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient with four months of urinary symptoms and six weeks of right hip and low back pain: examination, PSA and baseline tests, pain control, the staging and biopsy plan, and medical oncology referral. Concerns: He wants to know what the pain and the urinary symptoms mean, and to be told plainly; He wants to keep writing every morning and to carry on his duties as ambassador; He wants important discussions held in Spanish. [S]

tr.td: Multiparametric MRI of the prostate: gland 52 mL; 24 mm PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone from mid-gland to base with extraprostatic extension on the right; no seminal vesicle invasion; 13 mm right external iliac lymph node; abnormal marrow signal in the right iliac bone at the edge of the field

CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast: enlarged right external iliac (13 mm) and right obturator (11 mm) lymph nodes; sclerotic lesions in the right iliac wing and the L5 vertebral body without a soft-tissue mass or canal narrowing; no lung, liver or adrenal lesions

Whole-body bone scan (technetium-99m): two foci of increased uptake, in the right iliac wing and L5, matching the CT; no other skeletal lesions (fewer than four bone metastases, all in the spine and pelvis: low volume)

MRI-ultrasound fusion transperineal biopsy of the prostate, at the urology practice: adenocarcinoma, Gleason 4+4 (Grade Group 4) in 3 of 3 targeted cores (up to 80 percent of the core) and Gleason 4+4 or 4+3 in 6 of 12 systematic cores, all on the right; 9 of 14 cores in all; perineural invasion present; no intraductal or neuroendocrine features

Gallium-68 PSMA PET/CT: intense uptake in the right side of the prostate, in the right external iliac and right obturator nodes, and in the right iliac wing and L5; no other nodal, bone or visceral disease
Bone densitometry (DXA) of the hip and lumbar spine before androgen deprivation; L5 excluded because of a metastasis
Image-guided intensity-modulated radiotherapy to the prostate, 55 Gy in 20 daily fractions over four weeks, for low-volume metastatic disease; no pelvic nodal or bone radiation
Advance care planning conversation, about 30 minutes, in Spanish with a professional interpreter, with his consent

Bone metastases from prostate cancer: right iliac wing (painful) and L5 vertebral body; no cord compression: active, confirmed [S]
Pelvic lymph node metastases: right external iliac and right obturator nodes: active, confirmed [S]
Hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: active, confirmed [S]

Continuous androgen deprivation (leuprolide) with apalutamide, with monitoring of testosterone, PSA, thyroid function, blood pressure, glucose and lipids, bone health, rash, falls, hot flashes, sexual health, mood and cognition: active, confirmed [S]

Tobacco: never. Alcohol: wine with dinner a few evenings a week (AUDIT-C 2). No drug use [S]
Lives with his wife in the official residence; she is not named, is given no role in his care, and is not a source of history [S]
Activity: walks in the city most afternoons; many official dinners each week [S]
Insurance: an international health plan through his country's diplomatic service; the clinic documents his care with its usual U.S. conventions [S]
Strengths: a lifetime of disciplined daily writing, curiosity, a wide circle of friends, and an ease with hard conversations [S]

tr.td: New patient with four months of urinary symptoms and six weeks of right hip and low back pain: examination, PSA and baseline tests, pain control, the staging and biopsy plan, and medical oncology referral

Two-week review with the medical oncology consultation the same day: biopsy and staging results, the diagnosis, shared decision on treatment, the start of apalutamide, genetic testing, and bone density
Four-week review on apalutamide and leuprolide: early PSA response, testosterone, blood pressure, pain, the dental check and the first denosumab dose, and the radiotherapy plan
Three-month review: PSA and testosterone, thyroid function, blood count and chemistry, glucose, radiotherapy effects, the rash, the second leuprolide injection, and plans for the year
Same-day sick visit for an itchy rash on apalutamide
Medical oncology (genitourinary) consultation within two weeks for suspected metastatic prostate cancer: diagnosis, staging, systemic treatment, radiotherapy, bone health and genetic testing
Diagnosis and staging: multiparametric MRI of the prostate, an MRI-targeted transperineal biopsy at the urology practice, CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis, a bone scan, and PSMA PET/CT

Bone pain: acetaminophen 1000 mg up to three times a day; spinal cord compression warning signs explained in Spanish, with same-day assessment for new leg weakness or numbness, or loss of bladder or bowel control
Care in Spanish, his first language: a professional medical interpreter for every major discussion, written plans in Spanish, appointments placed around his morning writing and his official duties
Systemic therapy: apalutamide 240 mg daily from the consultation day and leuprolide 22.5 mg every twelve weeks from one week later, continuous; docetaxel not added for low-volume disease
Radiotherapy to the prostate, 55 Gy in 20 daily fractions, about six weeks after starting androgen deprivation, for low-volume metastatic disease
Germline genetic testing with pre-test counseling, and somatic testing of the biopsy tissue

Bone health on androgen deprivation: DXA and FRAX, cholecalciferol 1945 units a day, calcium 1000 to 1200 mg a day from food, weight-bearing exercise, a dental examination, then denosumab 60 mg every six months for high fracture risk; DXA again in one to two years

Monitoring on androgen deprivation and apalutamide: PSA and testosterone every three months, blood count and chemistry, TSH every four months, blood pressure at every visit, hemoglobin A1c and lipids, rash, falls, hot flashes, sexual health, fatigue, mood and cognition

Apalutamide rash: triamcinolone 0.1% cream twice daily for two weeks, cetirizine 10 mg daily, fragrance-free emollient, continue apalutamide; stop it and call the same day for blisters, peeling, mouth or eye sores, fever, or spread beyond a third of the skin
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily for primary prevention, with a lipid panel and ALT in six to twelve weeks
Diagnosis, staging and a shared treatment decision within three weeks of the first visit
Biopsy, CT, bone scan and PSMA PET/CT within ten days; apalutamide started at the consultation two weeks after intake
Bone pain controlled, with a pain score of 2 or less and sleep restored
Pain 6 of 10 at intake, 2 of 10 at four weeks on androgen deprivation
PSA of 0.2 ng/mL or less within about seven months of starting treatment
PSA 46.8 to 0.18 ng/mL at three months
Blood pressure below 130/80 mm Hg on androgen deprivation
152/90 at four weeks on apalutamide; 128/78 at the annual wellness visit on amlodipine 10 mg
Protect bone health: 25-hydroxyvitamin D of 30 ng/mL or more, calcium from food, weight-bearing exercise, and a bone-protective drug for high fracture risk
Denosumab given at four weeks after a dental check; vitamin D 28 ng/mL and rising; walking daily
Keep his morning writing and his official duties through treatment
Writing every morning; one week of official engagements postponed during radiotherapy
